equity.level_reason: Occupation is framed mainly through work conditions (route of exposure), so not read as SES. Table 1 reports prevalence by age, sex, race/ethnicity and education, described in text but not framed or quantified as disparities.

level_alternative.reason: If occupational group (e.g. white-collar vs other) is read as social position, the article frames 'health disparities among occupational groups' and quantifies them with aPRs (1.56, 1.55).

notes: Occupational group (22 SOC groups) is treated as a non-SPD exposure; if read as SES it would add a groupwise entry (per-group vs referent only, 22 groups) and occupational factors (workplace stress, shift rotation, organizational culture) as determinants. The Summary's claim that occupation is 'significantly associated' cites no omnibus test; significance rests on aPR CIs.
view_issues: Table 3 unweighted frequencies (e.g. 60,275 total) appear to be counts of all respondents per group, not adults meeting ≤2 CHMs as the header states. Text lists production (7.7%) among lowest though several groups are lower.
